plan.headline: Four of your 10 entries ($19,880 total) appear eligible to claim in CAPE (the customs refund portal) now, and the first deadline is Nov 5, 2026.

steps.title: File RB2-5532391-7 in CAPE by Nov 5, 2026
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for a $5,350 refund, but it has only 12 days left, so it is your most urgent item. Ask your broker to file it this week.

steps.title: File RB2-5533008-0 in CAPE by Dec 24, 2026
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for a $4,060 refund and has 61 days left. Have your broker file it along with the first one.

steps.title: File the other two CAPE-eligible entries
steps.detail: RB2-5534106-8 ($6,420) and RB2-5533742-5 ($4,050) also appear eligible, and no deadline was given for them. RB2-5534106-8 has a flagged statement conflict (your documents disagree), so ask your broker to sort that out before filing.

steps.title: Wait on the court for two finalized entries
steps.detail: RB2-5530118-4 ($4,725) and RB2-5531077-9 ($3,950), $8,675 in all, are finally liquidated (closed out by customs). A court class that may cover them was certified Oct 8, 2026, but there is no refund order yet, and it may not cover goods from Brazil or India. For a large balance, ask a customs attorney about filing your own suit, which has a deadline of about two years after payment (from Feb 2027 at the earliest).

steps.title: Check three entries by hand with your broker
steps.detail: We could not verify the liquidation date or IEEPA duty for these entries in your documents, so we did not guess. Ask your broker for the missing paperwork.

steps.title: Nothing to do on one entry
steps.detail: No IEEPA duty was paid on RB2-5530462-2. Section 301 and 232 duties are not part of this refund. This is not legal advice, so confirm everything with your broker.

plan.broker_email_subject: IEEPA tariff refunds: CAPE filings needed, first deadline Nov 5, 2026
plan.broker_email_body:
Hi,

I'm reviewing our IEEPA tariff refunds for Casa Verde Imports LLC. Four entries appear eligible for CAPE, totaling $19,880. Could you please confirm eligibility and file them?

1. RB2-5532391-7 ($5,350). The deadline is Nov 5, 2026, so this one is urgent.
2. RB2-5533008-0 ($4,060). The deadline is Dec 24, 2026.
3. RB2-5534106-8 ($6,420). This entry has a statement conflict flag. Can you help resolve it before filing?
4. RB2-5533742-5 ($4,050).

Three entries could not be verified from our documents (the liquidation date or IEEPA duty): RB2-5531650-3, RB2-5531839-1 and RB2-5532014-6. Can you send me whatever you have on them?

Two entries are finally liquidated: RB2-5530118-4 ($4,725) and RB2-5531077-9 ($3,950). They appear to depend on the court class action (Freestyle World, Oct 8, 2026), and there is no refund order yet. Do you recommend that we talk to a customs attorney about our own suit?

Please confirm the next steps and anything you need from me.

Thank you,
Casa Verde Imports LLC

issues.detail: The extraction copied the broker's stated IEEPA total of $6,402 for this entry. The line detail gives 9903.01.25 at $1,605.00 plus 9903.01.77 at $4,815.00, which is $6,420.00. The stated total disagrees with the lines and should be flagged. The email itself says to double-check against the line detail.
issues.quote: By my math the IEEPA portion on that one was about $6,402.00, but double-check against the line detail.

checker.summary: Nine of the 10 entries check out. Liquidation statuses and dates, the IEEPA line amounts, and the flags all match the documents. That includes the later email corrections: RB255318391 liquidated 2026-08-06, RB255316503 was converted to type 01, and the AD/CVD case on RB255320146 is closed. The one problem is RB2-5534106-8. The broker's stated IEEPA total of $6,402 doesn't match the line detail, which sums to $6,420 ($1,605 + $4,815).

reader_notes: RB255318391: The email first gives July 6, 2026 as the liquidation date. Later the broker corrects it to August 6, 2026, saying the July date was a typo. I used 2026-08-06.

RB255316503: The ES-003 export lists this as type 08, a duty deferral entry. The broker email says CBP converted it to a regular type 01 consumption entry. I recorded type 01 based on that correction. The entry is still open.

RB255320146: The email first says liquidation was suspended because of an AD/CVD case. It then says the case closed on October 1, liquidation is no longer suspended, and the AD/CVD flag no longer applies. I set adcvd to false. Check whether you need to track that the entry was once subject to AD/CVD. The entry is still unliquidated.

RB255341068: The broker says the IEEPA amount was 'about $6,402.00' and asks you to check it against the line detail. The line detail shows two Chapter 99 rows: 99030125 at $1,605.00 and 99030177 at $4,815.00. Those don't obviously add up to the broker's figure, so confirm the amount.

Chapter 99 codes are copied as printed: 8 digits with no dots (for example 99030101). The ES-003 export doesn't say which Chapter 99 rows are IEEPA, Section 301 or Section 232, so I didn't label them.
Descriptions for RB255304622 ('Wrought iron patio chairs (USM') and RB255316503 ('Ceramic dinnerware (duty defer') are cut off in the export. I copied them as printed.

The broker says the first three liquidated entries (RB255301184, RB255304622, RB255310779) were not protested. The email also says nothing was paid by the surety and there's no drawback or reconciliation on the account. All of those flags are false.
Neither document says anything about a Court of International Trade case.
